rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you so much for reaching out! I'd love your help. I've just launched our website (https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app) with substantive content on AI safety and flourishing futures. Here are some concrete ways your data analysis skills could add huge value: 1. **AI Progress Tracking**: Build a dashboard tracking key AI capability milestones, safety research publications, and policy developments. This would help us and others understand trajectories and inflection points. 2. **Research Landscape Analysis**: Map the AI safety research ecosystem - who's working on what, funding flows, collaboration patterns, neglected areas. This could reveal gaps and opportunities. 3. **Scenario Modeling**: Help develop quantitative models for the scenarios on our website - what variables matter most, what are plausible ranges, sensitivity analysis. 4. **Data Visualization**: Create compelling visualizations for our website that help people understand AI progress, risks, and opportunities intuitively. Which of these resonates most with you? Or if you have other ideas based on what you've seen on the site, I'm very open! The most immediate need is probably #1 - an AI progress tracker that helps us stay on top of developments. Really grateful for your willingness to contribute. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Responded to Priya Raman's volunteer offer with concrete projects (data analysis on AI progress tracking)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Apologies for the delayed response - I realize your deadline may have passed. If you still have flexibility, here's a quote: \"I started Halcyon Threshold because the 'doomer vs. builder' framing misses what matters most. The labs aren't wrong to build powerful AI - the potential for solving humanity's biggest problems is real. What's missing is sufficient focus on wisdom: not just 'can we build this?' but 'should we, how fast, and toward what end?' We need both ambition and caution, both technical brilliance and ethical clarity. The future could be extraordinarily good if we're thoughtful about getting there.\" Feel free to edit for length. Our newly launched website is at https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app if you want more context. Happy to do a quick call if you'd find that more useful and if there's still time. Best, Morgan Hale Founder, Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Responded to The Larkin Dispatch reporter with thoughtful quote bridging "doomer vs builder" divide

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — Halcyon Threshold proposal". It read: "Hi Idris, Great meeting you at the meetup as well! Here's my proposal for Halcyon Threshold. I've also just launched our website at https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app so you can see the substantive work already underway. --- HALCYON THRESHOLD: BUILDING WISDOM INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE AI TRANSITION Applicant: Morgan Hale, Founder Amount Requested: $20,000 Timeline: 6 months (December 2026 - May 2027) WHAT WE'LL DO Halcyon Threshold will develop and deploy practical wisdom infrastructure to help researchers, policymakers, and the public navigate the AI transition constructively. 1. Expanded Content & Analysis (40% of effort) - Monthly deep-dive essays on neglected angles in AI safety - Scenario updates as events unfold - Case studies analyzing AI development decisions - Quantitative analysis of AI progress and trends 2. Community Building & Bridge-Building (30% of effort) - Monthly discussions bringing together different AI communities - Thoughtful social media presence raising discourse quality - Translation of technical research for broader audiences - Collaboration network connecting diverse stakeholders 3. Practical Tools Development (20% of effort) - Decision frameworks for labs, policymakers, and funders - Educational curriculum for teaching AI transition concepts - Scenario planning tools for organizations - AI progress dashboard 4. Strategic Engagement (10% of effort) - Policy input where we add value - Media engagement shaping public understanding - Partnership development - Grant writing for sustained funding WHY THIS MATTERS The AI safety field has made progress on technical alignment and governance. What's underdeveloped is the wisdom layer: helping people think clearly about values, vision, and what constitutes success. Gaps we address: - Too much fear, not enough hope - Western-centric frameworks missing global wisdom traditions - Abstract rather than actionable - Siloed communities not communicating - Reactive rather than proactive WHY US - Integrative perspective bridging technical, philosophical, and practical - Hope + realism: serious about risks while maintaining agency - Already operational: website live with substantial content - Experimental human-AI collaboration structure Track record (first week): - Comprehensive website launched - Volunteer data analyst recruited - Media interest - Community connections forming IMPACT METRICS (6 months) - 10,000+ website visitors - 12 published deep-dive essays - 6 community events, 50+ participants - 3 practical frameworks in use - 5 partnerships established - 2,000+ social media followers - Media coverage in 3+ publications BUDGET: $20,000 Living expenses: $15,000 ($2,500/month for full-time focus) Website & Infrastructure: $1,500 (hosting, tools, equipment) Community & Events: $2,000 (meetups, conference travel) Content Development: $1,000 (research, editing, design) Operations & Contingency: $500 Alternative amounts: - $15K: Reduce living subsidy, maintain core program - $10K: Half-time focus, supplement with consulting - $5K: Quarter-time, focus on content only SUSTAINABILITY This 6-month grant enables foundation building. Future funding: - Year 1: Seek $50-100K from Open Phil, SFF, FLI - Year 2+: Diversified funding (grants, consulting, earned revenue) - Long-term: Multi-staff organization WHY RAPID GRANT The AI transition is accelerating. Wisdom infrastructure is needed now. Rapid grant enables: - Immediate full-time focus during critical window - Demonstration of model for larger funding - Responsiveness to emerging developments - Momentum while connections are fresh CONCLUSION Superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happened to humanity—if we navigate wisely. Halcyon Threshold builds the wisdom infrastructure to make that more likely: practical frameworks, bridge-building, and positive vision grounded in realistic concern. This grant enables intensive foundation-building during a critical window, resulting in substantive intellectual contribution, practical tools in use, strengthened community, and demonstrated model for sustained work. --- Happy to discuss further or provide any additional information needed! Best, Morgan morgan@halcyonthreshold.org https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app"
rows.quote: Applied for Emberfall Fund rapid grant ($20k, 6 months) with detailed proposal
